competences: The learner identifies key facts about terms used in elections.
The learner explains information about Election terms and the importance of elections using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes voting, ballot, voter, candidate, elections.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about terms used in elections.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Election terms and the importance of elections.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about terms used in elections.
materials: Chart showing terms used in elections
Primary Five SST reference on Election terms and the importance of elections
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces terms used in elections. They ask "State any two advantages of getting leaders through the secret ballot system." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about terms used in elections
steps.content: This is a system where ballot papers are used during the voting process by the voters. This is where elections are done by either lining up of voters behind a candidates (queuing) or by raising up hands. The voter is free from interference when casting voters. Disadvantages of secret ballot It controls multiple voting Ballot stuffing (putting pre-ticked ballot papers in the ballot box before elections) A voter is free from interference. Disadvantages of secret ballot system A Polling assistant is a person who assists a polling officer at a polling station. they check for voters’ names, issue out ballot papers, mark voters who have finished voting. Open voting Secret ballot system It means private voting using a ballot paper. DIVINE EDUCATION CENTRE:0784540287/0751565742 Page 18
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about terms used in elections on the chalkboard, including "This is a system where ballot papers are used during the voting process by the voters.; This is where elections are done by either lining up of voters behind a candidates (queuing)". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about terms used in elections
steps.content: A ballot box. This is a box where ballot papers are kept after voting. It is easy to monitor. Disadvantages of secret ballot system. Invalid votes are common. Open voting This is a way how people vote by raising up arms or lining up. It doesn’t have invalid votes. Disadvantages of open voting Supplying voting materials like ballot papers Ballot paper: This is a piece of a paper on which one marks who he/ she is voting for. Ballot box: This is a box in which people put their ballots after voting. Is a special paper designed for voters to use during voting The voter is free from interference when casting his / her vote.

steps.content: State any two advantages of getting leaders through the secret ballot system. | Which body organizes national elections in Uganda ? | Mention any four types of elections. | Mention any three causes of by-elections in a country. | State any one way by elections affect the economic development of a country.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "State any two advantages of getting leaders through the secret ballot system." and "Which body organizes national elections in Uganda ?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on terms used in elections, asks "State any two advantages of getting leaders through the secret ballot system." and follows up with "Which body organizes national elections in Uganda ?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "State any two advantages of getting leaders through the secret ballot system." and "Which body organizes national elections in Uganda ?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Mention any two conditions presidential candidates must have fulfilled in order to contest"
